sanskrit: yamas tu taṃ tathā baddhvā prayāto dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ sāvitrī cāpi duḥkhārtā yamam evānvagacchata niyamavratasaṃsiddhā mahābhāgā pativratā
english: Yama, having thus bound him, departed facing southward; and Sāvitrī too, tormented by grief, followed Yama himself — she who was perfected in vows and observances, the greatly blessed devoted wife.

sanskrit: yama uvāca nivarta gaccha sāvitri kuruṣvāsyaurdhvadehikam kṛtaṃ bhartus tvayānṛṇyaṃ yāvad gamyaṃ gataṃ tvayā
english: Yama said: Turn back, go, Sāvitrī; perform the post-mortem rites for him. Your debt to your husband has been paid; you have gone as far as one may go.

sanskrit: sāvitry uvāca yatra me nīyate bhartā svayaṃ vā yatra gacchati mayāpi tatra gantavyam eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Sāvitrī said: Where my husband is led, or where he himself goes, I too must go there — this is the eternal law.

sanskrit: tapasā guruvṛttyā ca bhartuḥ snehād vratena ca tava caiva prasādena na me pratihatā gatiḥ
english: Through austerity, devoted service to the teacher, love for my husband, and through vows, and by your own grace, my path is not obstructed.

sanskrit: prāhuḥ saptapadaṃ mitraṃ budhās tattvārthadarśinaḥ mitratāṃ ca puraskṛtya kiṃ cid vakṣyāmi tac chṛṇu
english: The wise who perceive the truth of things declare that seven steps together make a friendship; honouring that friendship, I shall say something — listen to it.

sanskrit: nānātmavantas tu vane caranti; dharmaṃ ca vāsaṃ ca pariśramaṃ ca vijñānato dharmam udāharanti; tasmāt santo dharmam āhuḥ pradhānam
english: Those of various natures wander in the forest, enduring dharma, dwelling, and hardship; the wise declare dharma through understanding; therefore the good say dharma is paramount.

sanskrit: ekasya dharmeṇa satāṃ matena; sarve sma taṃ mārgam anuprapannāḥ mā vai dvitīyaṃ mā tṛtīyaṃ ca vāñche; tasmāt santo dharmam āhuḥ pradhānam
english: By the dharma of the one, by the conviction of the good, all of us enter that path; let no one desire a second or a third; therefore the good say dharma is paramount.

sanskrit: yama uvāca nivarta tuṣṭo 'smi tavānayā girā; svarākṣaravyañjanahetuyuktayā varaṃ vṛṇīṣveha vināsya jīvitaṃ; dadāni te sarvam anindite varam
english: Yama said: Turn back — I am pleased by this speech of yours, composed of excellent syllables, letters, and logic; choose a boon here, excepting this one's life; I grant you any boon, blameless one.

sanskrit: sāvitry uvāca cyutaḥ svarājyād vanavāsam āśrito; vinaṣṭacakṣuḥ śvaśuro mamāśrame sa labdhacakṣur balavān bhaven nṛpas; tava prasādāj jvalanārkasaṃnibhaḥ
english: Sāvitrī said: My father-in-law, fallen from his own kingdom and dwelling in the forest, his eyes destroyed, lives in the hermitage; may he by your grace regain his sight, becoming a powerful king, blazing like fire and sun.

sanskrit: yama uvāca dadāni te sarvam anindite varaṃ; yathā tvayoktaṃ bhavitā ca tat tathā tavādhvanā glānim ivopalakṣaye; nivarta gacchasva na te śramo bhavet
english: Yama said: I grant you all of this boon, blameless one; it shall be as you have said. I perceive what seems like weariness in your path; turn back, go — let there be no fatigue for you.

sanskrit: sāvitry uvāca kutaḥ śramo bhartṛsamīpato hi me; yato hi bhartā mama sā gatir dhruvā yatra patiṃ neṣyasi tatra me gatiḥ; sureśa bhūyaś ca vaco nibodha me
english: Sāvitrī said: How can there be weariness for me near my husband? For where my husband is, that is my certain course; wherever you will lead my lord, there is my path. O lord of the gods, hear yet another word from me.

sanskrit: satāṃ sakṛt saṃgatam īpsitaṃ paraṃ; tataḥ paraṃ mitram iti pracakṣate na cāphalaṃ satpuruṣeṇa saṃgataṃ; tataḥ satāṃ saṃnivaset samāgame
english: A single meeting with the good is supremely desired; beyond that, it is called true friendship; association with a virtuous person is never fruitless; therefore one should dwell in the company of the good.

sanskrit: yama uvāca manonukūlaṃ budhabuddhivardhanaṃ; tvayāham ukto vacanaṃ hitāśrayam vinā punaḥ satyavato 'sya jīvitaṃ; varaṃ dvitīyaṃ varayasva bhāmini
english: Yama said: You have spoken to me words pleasing to the mind, increasing the wisdom of the wise, conducive to welfare — again excepting the life of this Satyavan; choose a second boon, passionate lady.

sanskrit: sāvitry uvāca hṛtaṃ purā me śvaśurasya dhīmataḥ; svam eva rājyaṃ sa labheta pārthivaḥ jahyāt svadharmaṃ na ca me gurur yathā; dvitīyam etaṃ varayāmi te varam
english: Sāvitrī said: The kingdom of my wise father-in-law was stolen of old; may that king regain his own realm, and may my venerable father-in-law never abandon his own dharma — this second boon I ask of you.

sanskrit: yama uvāca svam eva rājyaṃ pratipatsyate 'cirān; na ca svadharmāt parihāsyate nṛpaḥ kṛtena kāmena mayā nṛpātmaje; nivarta gacchasva na te śramo bhavet
english: Yama said: He shall soon regain his own kingdom; the king shall not be separated from his own dharma — this wish is granted by me, O daughter of a king; turn back, go, let there be no fatigue for you.

sanskrit: sāvitry uvāca prajās tvayemā niyamena saṃyatā; niyamya caitā nayase na kāmayā ato yamatvaṃ tava deva viśrutaṃ; nibodha cemāṃ giram īritāṃ mayā
english: Sāvitrī said: These creatures are restrained by you through law; having restrained them you lead them, not from desire — thus your lordship as Yama, O god, is renowned; hear also this word spoken by me.

sanskrit: adrohaḥ sarvabhūteṣu karmaṇā manasā girā anugrahaś ca dānaṃ ca satāṃ dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Non-malice toward all beings in deed, thought, and speech, along with benevolence and giving — this is the eternal dharma of the good.

sanskrit: evaṃprāyaś ca loko 'yaṃ manuṣyāḥ śaktipeśalāḥ santas tv evāpy amitreṣu dayāṃ prāpteṣu kurvate
english: Such indeed is this world — human beings are delicate in their power; yet even the good show compassion toward enemies when they are in distress.

sanskrit: yama uvāca pipāsitasyeva yathā bhavet payas; tathā tvayā vākyam idaṃ samīritam vinā punaḥ satyavato 'sya jīvitaṃ; varaṃ vṛṇīṣveha śubhe yad icchasi
english: Yama said: As water is to one who thirsts, so has this speech been uttered by you; again excepting the life of this Satyavan, choose here whatever boon you wish, auspicious one.

sanskrit: sāvitry uvāca mamānapatyaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ pitā; bhavet pituḥ putraśataṃ mamaurasam kulasya saṃtānakaraṃ ca yad bhavet; tṛtīyam etaṃ varayāmi te varam
english: Sāvitrī said: My father, the lord of the earth, is without offspring; may there be a hundred sons born of my father himself, continuing the lineage of his family — this third boon I ask of you.

sanskrit: yama uvāca kulasya saṃtānakaraṃ suvarcasaṃ; śataṃ sutānāṃ pitur astu te śubhe kṛtena kāmena narādhipātmaje; nivarta dūraṃ hi pathas tvam āgatā
english: Yama said: A hundred sons of your father, continuing the lineage, of great splendour — may they be yours, auspicious one; this wish is granted, O daughter of a king; turn back — you have come a long way.

sanskrit: sāvitry uvāca na dūram etan mama bhartṛsaṃnidhau; mano hi me dūrataraṃ pradhāvati tathā vrajann eva giraṃ samudyatāṃ; mayocyamānāṃ śṛṇu bhūya eva ca
english: Sāvitrī said: This is not far for me when near my husband; for my mind races even farther ahead; thus even as you walk, listen once more to the words I am ready to speak.

sanskrit: vivasvatas tvaṃ tanayaḥ pratāpavāṃs; tato hi vaivasvata ucyase budhaiḥ śamena dharmeṇa ca rañjitāḥ prajās; tatas taveheśvara dharmarājatā
english: You are the glorious son of Vivasvat; therefore the wise call you Vaivasvata; the creatures are won over by your peace and dharma — hence, O lord, you hold here the kingship of dharma.

sanskrit: ātmany api na viśvāsas tāvān bhavati satsu yaḥ tasmāt satsu viśeṣeṇa sarvaḥ praṇayam icchati
english: Even in oneself there is not as much trust as there is in the good; therefore everyone especially desires affection from the good.

sanskrit: sauhṛdāt sarvabhūtānāṃ viśvāso nāma jāyate tasmāt satsu viśeṣeṇa viśvāsaṃ kurute janaḥ
english: From the goodwill of all beings, trust is born; therefore people especially place their trust in the good.

sanskrit: yama uvāca udāhṛtaṃ te vacanaṃ yad aṅgane; śubhe na tādṛk tvad ṛte mayā śrutam anena tuṣṭo 'smi vināsya jīvitaṃ; varaṃ caturthaṃ varayasva gaccha ca
english: Yama said: The words you have uttered, O slender-waisted, auspicious one — such have not been heard by me from any other; by these I am pleased; excepting this one's life, choose a fourth boon and go.

sanskrit: sāvitry uvāca mamātmajaṃ satyavatas tathaurasaṃ; bhaved ubhābhyām iha yat kulodvaham śataṃ sutānāṃ balavīryaśālinām; idaṃ caturthaṃ varayāmi te varam
english: Sāvitrī said: May there be born sons of my own body from Satyavan, a hundred sons bearing strength and valour, upholding both our families here — this fourth boon I ask of you.

sanskrit: yama uvāca śataṃ sutānāṃ balavīryaśālināṃ; bhaviṣyati prītikaraṃ tavābale pariśramas te na bhaven nṛpātmaje; nivarta dūraṃ hi pathas tvam āgatā
english: Yama said: A hundred sons bearing strength and valour shall be born to your delight, gentle one; let there be no weariness for you, O daughter of a king; turn back — you have come a long way.

sanskrit: sāvitry uvāca satāṃ sadā śāśvatī dharmavṛttiḥ; santo na sīdanti na ca vyathanti satāṃ sadbhir nāphalaḥ saṃgamo 'sti; sadbhyo bhayaṃ nānuvartanti santaḥ
english: Sāvitrī said: The conduct in dharma of the good is always eternal; the good neither sink nor tremble; association with the good is never fruitless; the good do not follow fear from the good.

sanskrit: santo hi satyena nayanti sūryaṃ; santo bhūmiṃ tapasā dhārayanti santo gatir bhūtabhavyasya rājan; satāṃ madhye nāvasīdanti santaḥ
english: For the good guide the sun by truth; the good uphold the earth through austerity; the good are the course of the past and the future, O king; among the good, the good do not sink.

sanskrit: āryajuṣṭam idaṃ vṛttam iti vijñāya śāśvatam santaḥ parārthaṃ kurvāṇā nāvekṣante pratikriyām
english: Knowing this conduct to be eternal, honoured by the noble, the good, acting for the sake of others, do not look for any return.

sanskrit: na ca prasādaḥ satpuruṣeṣu mogho; na cāpy artho naśyati nāpi mānaḥ yasmād etan niyataṃ satsu nityaṃ; tasmāt santo rakṣitāro bhavanti
english: Grace bestowed upon the virtuous is never wasted; neither wealth nor honour is lost; because this is certain and constant among the good — therefore the good become protectors.

sanskrit: yama uvāca yathā yathā bhāṣasi dharmasaṃhitaṃ; manonukūlaṃ supadaṃ mahārthavat tathā tathā me tvayi bhaktir uttamā; varaṃ vṛṇīṣvāpratimaṃ yatavrate
english: Yama said: The more you speak words combined with dharma, pleasing to the mind, well-formed and full of great meaning, the more my supreme devotion grows toward you; choose an incomparable boon, O lady of firm vows.

sanskrit: sāvitry uvāca na te 'pavargaḥ sukṛtād vinākṛtas; tathā yathānyeṣu vareṣu mānada varaṃ vṛṇe jīvatu satyavān ayaṃ; yathā mṛtā hy evam ahaṃ vinā patim
english: Sāvitrī said: Your release from meritorious action does not happen without being granted, O giver of honour, as in the other boons; I choose this boon: let this Satyavan live — for without my husband I am as if dead.

sanskrit: na kāmaye bhartṛvinākṛtā sukhaṃ; na kāmaye bhartṛvinākṛtā divam na kāmaye bhartṛvinākṛtā śriyaṃ; na bhartṛhīnā vyavasāmi jīvitum
english: I do not desire happiness bereft of my husband; I do not desire heaven bereft of my husband; I do not desire prosperity bereft of my husband; I do not resolve to live as one without a husband.

sanskrit: varātisargaḥ śataputratā mama; tvayaiva datto hriyate ca me patiḥ varaṃ vṛṇe jīvatu satyavān ayaṃ; tavaiva satyaṃ vacanaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: The grant of the boon — my having a hundred sons — was given by you yourself, yet my husband is being taken away; I choose the boon: let this Satyavan live; thus your own word will be true.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tathety uktvā tu tān pāśān muktvā vaivasvato yamaḥ dharmarājaḥ prahṛṣṭātmā sāvitrīm idam abravīt
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Having said "So be it" and releasing those bonds, Yama Vaivasvata, the king of dharma, his soul filled with joy, spoke these words to Sāvitrī:

sanskrit: eṣa bhadre mayā mukto bhartā te kulanandini arogas tava neyaś ca siddhārthaś ca bhaviṣyati
english: "This husband of yours, auspicious one, delighter of your family, has been released by me; free from disease, he will lead you and his purposes shall be fulfilled."

sanskrit: caturvarṣaśataṃ cāyus tvayā sārdham avāpsyati iṣṭvā yajñaiś ca dharmeṇa khyātiṃ loke gamiṣyati
english: "He shall attain a lifespan of four hundred years together with you; having performed sacrifices with dharma, he shall gain renown in the world."

sanskrit: tvayi putraśataṃ caiva satyavāñ janayiṣyati te cāpi sarve rājānaḥ kṣatriyāḥ putrapautriṇaḥ khyātās tvannāmadheyāś ca bhaviṣyantīha śāśvatāḥ
english: "Satyavan shall beget on you a hundred sons; all of them shall be kings, warriors, with sons and grandsons, renowned and bearing your name — they shall be eternal here."

sanskrit: pituś ca te putraśataṃ bhavitā tava mātari mālavyāṃ mālavā nāma śāśvatāḥ putrapautriṇaḥ bhrātaras te bhaviṣyanti kṣatriyās tridaśopamāḥ
english: "And a hundred sons shall be born to your father by your mother, of the Mālava lineage — Mālavas by name, eternal, with sons and grandsons; they shall be your brothers, warriors equal to the thirty gods."

sanskrit: evaṃ tasyai varaṃ dattvā dharmarājaḥ pratāpavān nivartayitvā sāvitrīṃ svam eva bhavanaṃ yayau
english: Having thus granted the boons to her, the glorious king of dharma, turning Sāvitrī back, went to his own abode.

sanskrit: sāvitry api yame yāte bhartāraṃ pratilabhya ca jagāma tatra yatrāsyā bhartuḥ śāvaṃ kalevaram
english: And Sāvitrī too, when Yama had departed and she had recovered her husband, went to where the lifeless body of her husband lay.

sanskrit: sā bhūmau prekṣya bhartāram upasṛtyopagūhya ca utsaṅge śira āropya bhūmāv upaviveśa ha
english: Seeing her husband on the ground, she approached and embraced him, and placing his head in her lap, she sat down on the earth.

sanskrit: saṃjñāṃ ca satyavāṃl labdhvā sāvitrīm abhyabhāṣata proṣyāgata iva premṇā punaḥ punar udīkṣya vai
english: And Satyavan, having regained consciousness, spoke to Sāvitrī; gazing at her again and again with affection, as if returned from a journey.

sanskrit: satyavān uvāca suciraṃ bata supto 'smi kimarthaṃ nāvabodhitaḥ kva cāsau puruṣaḥ śyāmo yo 'sau māṃ saṃcakarṣa ha
english: Satyavan said: "Alas, I have slept very long — why was I not awakened? And where is that dark man who was dragging me away?"

sanskrit: sāvitry uvāca suciraṃ bata supto 'si mamāṅke puruṣarṣabha gataḥ sa bhagavān devaḥ prajāsaṃyamano yamaḥ
english: Sāvitrī said: "Alas, you have slept very long on my lap, O bull among men; that blessed god who restrains the creatures, Yama, has gone."

sanskrit: viśrānto 'si mahābhāga vinidraś ca nṛpātmaja yadi śakyaṃ samuttiṣṭha vigāḍhāṃ paśya śarvarīm
english: "You are rested, O greatly fortunate one, and free from sleep, O son of a king; if you are able, rise up and behold the deep night."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca upalabhya tataḥ saṃjñāṃ sukhasupta ivotthitaḥ diśaḥ sarvā vanāntāṃś ca nirīkṣyovāca satyavān
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then, having regained his senses, he rose as if from a pleasant sleep; gazing at all the directions and the edges of the forest, Satyavan spoke:

sanskrit: phalāhāro 'smi niṣkrāntas tvayā saha sumadhyame tataḥ pāṭayataḥ kāṣṭhaṃ śiraso me rujābhavat
english: "I went out to gather fruits with you, O slender-waisted one; then, while splitting wood, a pain arose in my head."

sanskrit: śirobhitāpasaṃtaptaḥ sthātuṃ ciram aśaknuvan tavotsaṅge prasupto 'ham iti sarvaṃ smare śubhe
english: "Scorched by the burning heat in my head, unable to stand for long, I fell asleep in your lap — all this I remember, auspicious one."

sanskrit: tvayopagūḍhasya ca me nidrayāpahṛtaṃ manaḥ tato 'paśyaṃ tamo ghoraṃ puruṣaṃ ca mahaujasam
english: "And while being embraced by you, my mind was carried away by sleep; then I saw terrible darkness and a man of great radiance."

sanskrit: tad yadi tvaṃ vijānāsi kiṃ tad brūhi sumadhyame svapno me yadi vā dṛṣṭo yadi vā satyam eva tat
english: "If you know what that was, tell me, O slender-waisted one — whether it was a dream I saw, or whether it was real indeed."

sanskrit: tam uvācātha sāvitrī rajanī vyavagāhate śvas te sarvaṃ yathāvṛttam ākhyāsyāmi nṛpātmaja
english: Then Sāvitrī said to him: "The night is deepening; tomorrow, O son of a king, I shall tell you everything exactly as it occurred."

sanskrit: uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhadraṃ te pitarau paśya suvrata vigāḍhā rajanī ceyaṃ nivṛttaś ca divākaraḥ
english: "Rise up, rise up — may good come to you; see your parents, O one of pure vows; this night is deep and the day-maker has departed."

sanskrit: naktaṃcarāś caranty ete hṛṣṭāḥ krūrābhibhāṣiṇaḥ śrūyante parṇaśabdāś ca mṛgāṇāṃ caratāṃ vane
english: "These night-wanderers roam about, joyful and uttering fierce cries; the sounds of leaves and of animals roaming in the forest are heard."

sanskrit: etāḥ śivā ghoranādā diśaṃ dakṣiṇapaścimām āsthāya viruvanty ugrāḥ kampayantyo mano mama
english: "These jackals, with their terrible cries, taking up the south-western direction, howl fiercely, shaking my heart."

sanskrit: satyavān uvāca vanaṃ pratibhayākāraṃ ghanena tamasā vṛtam na vijñāsyasi panthānaṃ gantuṃ caiva na śakṣyasi
english: Satyavan said: "The forest appears terrifying, wrapped in dense darkness; you will not be able to discern the path, and you will not be able to go."

sanskrit: sāvitry uvāca asminn adya vane dagdhe śuṣkavṛkṣaḥ sthito jvalan vāyunā dhamyamāno 'gnir dṛśyate 'tra kva cit kva cit
english: Sāvitrī said: "In this forest that was burned today, a dry tree stands blazing; fanned by the wind, fire is visible here and there."

sanskrit: tato 'gnim ānayitveha jvālayiṣyāmi sarvataḥ kāṣṭhānīmāni santīha jahi saṃtāpam ātmanaḥ
english: "Then, having brought fire here, I shall kindle it on all sides; there is wood here — cast off the anguish of your heart."

sanskrit: yadi notsahase gantuṃ sarujaṃ tvābhilakṣaye na ca jñāsyasi panthānaṃ tamasā saṃvṛte vane
english: "If you are not able to go, I observe that you are in pain; and you will not know the path in the forest covered by darkness."

sanskrit: śvaḥ prabhāte vane dṛśye yāsyāvo 'numate tava vasāveha kṣapām etāṃ rucitaṃ yadi te 'nagha
english: "Tomorrow at dawn, when the forest is visible, we shall go with your consent; let us stay here this night, if it pleases you, O sinless one."

sanskrit: satyavān uvāca śirorujā nivṛttā me svasthāny aṅgāni lakṣaye mātāpitṛbhyām icchāmi saṃgamaṃ tvatprasādajam
english: Satyavan said: "The pain in my head has subsided; I perceive my limbs to be well; I wish to meet my mother and father — and this meeting is born of your grace."

sanskrit: na kadā cid vikāle hi gatapūrvo mayāśramaḥ anāgatāyāṃ saṃdhyāyāṃ mātā me praruṇaddhi mām
english: "Never before have I gone to the hermitage at an improper time; my mother stops me whenever the evening has not yet come."

sanskrit: divāpi mayi niṣkrānte saṃtapyete gurū mama vicinoti ca māṃ tātaḥ sahaivāśramavāsibhiḥ
english: "Even when I go out during the day, both my venerable parents are distressed; my father searches for me together with the hermitage-dwellers."

sanskrit: mātrā pitrā ca subhṛśaṃ duḥkhitābhyām ahaṃ purā upālabdhaḥ subahuśaś cireṇāgacchasīti ha
english: "By my mother and father, greatly afflicted, I have often been reproached in the past: 'You have come back late.'"

sanskrit: kā tv avasthā tayor adya madartham iti cintaye tayor adṛśye mayi ca mahad duḥkhaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: "What is their condition today on my account, I think; when I am unseen by them, great sorrow will befall them."

sanskrit: purā mām ūcatuś caiva rātrāv asrāyamāṇakau bhṛśaṃ suduḥkhitau vṛddhau bahuśaḥ prītisaṃyutau
english: "They used to speak to me before as well, not tearful in the night, greatly afflicted, the two elders, many times full of affection:"

sanskrit: tvayā hīnau na jīvāva muhūrtam api putraka yāvad dhariṣyase putra tāvan nau jīvitaṃ dhruvam
english: "'Without you we cannot live even for a moment, my son; as long as you shall live, my son, for that long our life is certain.'"

sanskrit: vṛddhayor andhayor yaṣṭis tvayi vaṃśaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ tvayi piṇḍaś ca kīrtiś ca saṃtānaṃ cāvayor iti
english: "'You are the staff of two old blind people; in you the lineage is established; in you rest our funeral offerings, our renown, and our continuity.'"

sanskrit: mātā vṛddhā pitā vṛddhas tayor yaṣṭir ahaṃ kila tau rātrau mām apaśyantau kām avasthāṃ gamiṣyataḥ
english: "My mother is old, my father is old, and I am their staff; not seeing me this night, what condition will those two come to?"

sanskrit: nidrāyāś cābhyasūyāmi yasyā hetoḥ pitā mama mātā ca saṃśayaṃ prāptā matkṛte 'napakāriṇī
english: "And I am angry at sleep, on account of which my father and my innocent mother have come to uncertainty because of me."

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca saṃśayaṃ prāptaḥ kṛcchrām āpadam āsthitaḥ mātāpitṛbhyāṃ hi vinā nāhaṃ jīvitum utsahe
english: "And I myself have come to uncertainty, fallen into terrible danger; for without my mother and father I do not resolve to live."

sanskrit: vyaktam ākulayā buddhyā prajñācakṣuḥ pitā mama ekaikam asyāṃ velāyāṃ pṛcchaty āśramavāsinam
english: "Clearly my father, whose sight is wisdom, with an agitated mind, at this very hour questions each hermitage-dweller one by one."

sanskrit: nātmānam anuśocāmi yathāhaṃ pitaraṃ śubhe bhartāraṃ cāpy anugatāṃ mātaraṃ paridurbalām
english: "I do not grieve for myself as much as I grieve for my father, O auspicious one, and for my mother who has followed her husband and is utterly frail."

sanskrit: matkṛtena hi tāv adya saṃtāpaṃ param eṣyataḥ jīvantāv anujīvāmi bhartavyau tau mayeti ha tayoḥ priyaṃ me kartavyam iti jīvāmi cāpy aham
english: "For on my account the two of them shall today reach the greatest anguish; as long as they live I live after them — they are to be supported by me; thinking 'I must do what is dear to them,' I too live."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca evam uktvā sa dharmātmā guruvartī gurupriyaḥ ucchritya bāhū duḥkhārtaḥ sasvaraṃ praruroda ha
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Having spoken thus, that righteous-souled one, devoted to his elders and dear to them, raised his arms and, tormented by grief, wept aloud.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīt tathā dṛṣṭvā bhartāraṃ śokakarśitam pramṛjyāśrūṇi netrābhyāṃ sāvitrī dharmacāriṇī
english: Then, seeing her husband thus emaciated by grief, Sāvitrī the dharma-walking one, wiping the tears from his eyes, spoke:

sanskrit: yadi me 'sti tapas taptaṃ yadi dattaṃ hutaṃ yadi śvaśrūśvaśurabhartṝṇāṃ mama puṇyās tu śarvarī
english: "If austerity has been practiced by me, if gifts have been given, if oblations have been offered — may this night be auspicious for my mother-in-law, father-in-law, and husband."

sanskrit: na smarāmy uktapūrvāṃ vai svaireṣv apy anṛtāṃ giram tena satyena tāv adya dhriyetāṃ śvaśurau mama
english: "I do not recall having ever spoken an untruth even in casual matters; by that truth, may both my parents-in-law be sustained today."
